title: GeoJSON Geometry Type Counter: The Mix
description: Count Points, LineStrings, Polygons and other geometry types in a FeatureCollection with the GeoJSON Geometry Type Counter. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a four-feature sample reports Point 2, LineString 1, Polygon 1 — the mix that tells you the file is a site plan, not a boundary set, before you draw a single thing.
quick_answer: The GeoJSON Geometry Type Counter counts how many features of each geometry type a GeoJSON object holds — Points, LineStrings, Polygons and their Multi- forms. Paste the file and read the breakdown: the composition report that tells renderers, importers and reviewers what kind of geography they are actually dealing with.

body.t: GIS layers are typed: points to the point layer, polygons to the polygon layer. The type census is the routing table for a mixed file’s import. The total it must reconcile with is the
A style written for polygons meeting a file of points fails quietly. Count types before wiring styles, and the silence never happens.
‘Delivery will contain building polygons only’ is verifiable: any Point in the census is a breach with a number on it.
CSV exports points honestly; lines and polygons need other paths. The mix tells you which parts of a file a
A ‘parcels’ file reporting Polygon 0, Point 412 is not a parcels file — it is parcel centroids wearing a parcels filename. Zeros in the census are findings, not absences.

examples.label: Example · Multi- forms are their own types

body.t: MultiPolygon is counted as MultiPolygon, not as several Polygons — the type is the geometry’s declared shape, and conflating them corrupts layer planning.

popular_table.title: The seven geometry types
popular_table.note: Null geometry is counted as its own honest category when it appears — a feature can exist with geometry: null, and a census that hides them lies by omission.

faq: As GeometryCollection features at the top level — with their member geometries being separate citizens. Tools differ on nested counting; this census counts features by their geometry’s declared type, collections included as themselves.
Reported as null/none rather than silently skipped — a delivery heavy with nulls is a story the census should tell.
Types, not vertices — the Coordinate Counter holds that census. Together they describe a file’s cast and its crowd.
A feature has exactly one geometry (or null) — the mix lives across features, which is what makes the per-type census well-defined.
Altitude does not change type: a Point with three numbers is a Point. The census reads the type field, not the position length.
No — counting types is not validating geometry. A self-intersecting Polygon still counts as a Polygon; validity is another gate.
Can it split a file by type?
Counting advises the split; GIS performs it. Knowing the mix sizes each output layer before you build it.
